name: praise
description: Communicating a sincere positive appraisal about qualities or actions of something or someone.
perceptions: That thing or person has an aspect or doing something that I find appealing.
results: Maybe you'll communicate your praise, or maybe you'll keep it to yourself.
examples: Movie gets a good review by a film critic.
Giving your employee positive feedback on a project.
Taking your kid out for ice cream after the doing well on the test.

guidance.description: These articles have advice that may help praise more authentic and effective.

variations.name: receiving praise
variations.description: A perception that someone has judged one of your characteristics or actions in a positive way.
perceptions: Someone has communicated something positive about me or someone close.
desires: desire to be perceived a certain way
results: If you agree with the praise, you may feel a rush of positive reward chemicals.
If you disagree with the praise, you may feel guilty about receiving it.
You may be anxious that it just sets the bar higher for next time.
examples: Your boss gives you positive feedback on the project.
Your teenage thanks you for being fair.

guidance.description: Here are some references that may help deal more gracefully with praise.

variations.name: flattering
variations.description: Communicating a positive appraisal about qualities or actions of something or someone with the aim of gaining favor with them.
perceptions: I would like to improve my relationship wit that person.
I'll let them know something nice about them.
results: Maybe the person will be impressed by the praise, or maybe they'll be suspicious.
examples: Employee tells the boss she looks good.
Politician tells the audience they're all awesome.

guidance.description: Flattery is a type of white lie, but why would it be a problem? Doesn’t everyone like to be told good things about themselves? Sure, but false praise is not the same as a thoughtful, honest compliment.

comparisons.description: 'Flattery' is insincere 'praise' done to score points with someone.

variations.name: receiving flattery
variations.description: A sense that someone has judged you positively in a way that indicated they may want something from you.
perceptions: Someone has communicated something positive about me or someone close.
The context of this praise is a little off.
I wonder what they really want.
desires: desire to be perceived a certain way
examples: Your employee compliments you just before performance reviews.
The politician appreciates your thoughtful feedback just before the election.

guidance.description: Here are some references that may help deal with suspected flattery.

commentaries.quote: Praise is warming and desirable, what the human race lives on like bread. But praise is an earned thing.
A man who flatters his neighbor spreads a net for his feet.
Undeserved praise, is satire in disguise.
Nothing is more effective than sincere, accurate praise, and nothing is more lame than a cookie-cutter compliment.
Blessed is he who has learned to admire but not envy, to follow but not imitate, to praise but not flatter, and to lead but not manipulate.
God doesn’t want our flattery. He wants our heartfelt praise every day about what we remember, what we attribute, and what we retell.
Nobody gets praised for the right reasons.
In the best, the friendliest and simplest relations flattery or praise is necessary, just as grease is necessary to keep wheels turning.
